Quantum computing consulting firms fall into five types: global strategy and technology services firms, vendors’ services arms, specialist advisers, security and cryptography specialists, and academic or national laboratory groups. Pick the type by the decision you face, then test the firm on its method, its independence and what it says it will not cover.

The five types of quantum consulting firm

These groups are TQI’s view, built from the way buyers describe their options. They overlap, and many organizations use two or three over the life of a program. The TQI consulting page sorts providers into four of these groups; security specialists are added here because the migration to post-quantum cryptography is a separate buying decision.

Ten questions to ask any quantum consulting firm

  1. What decision will this change, and what will I hold at the end? Ask for the output in one page before you sign.
  2. What data does the analysis start from, and can I see the method? A documented method names its sources, sample sizes and limits. QED-C’s methodology for its 2025 industry report is an example: it lists its data sources, states survey samples of 115 and 100 respondents and has a section on data limitations.
  3. What is each claim measured against? HSBC’s headline result is up to 34 percent better than “common classical techniques”, which is a best case against a stated baseline (HSBC release). Ask for the same clarity.
  4. Who does the work? Ask for names, qualifications and time on the project.
  5. What commercial relationships could affect the advice? Ask about vendor partnerships, investments and data or media businesses.
  6. Can you show a public deliverable? Government reports are a useful test. The UK Department for Transport’s quantum transport study is public and says that any attempt to quantify impacts rests on many assumptions.
  7. What will you not cover? The answer shows where the firm’s depth ends.
  8. How do you handle uncertainty about timing? Be cautious of confident dates for when a capability will arrive.
  9. For security work, do you start with a cryptographic inventory? The BIS’s roadmap begins there, followed by cryptographic agility and phased migration, and NIST has published three post-quantum standards to plan against.
  10. What happens after delivery? Ask whether the analysis will be refreshed and who answers questions in six months.

Warning signs

  • A single vendor’s roadmap presented as a neutral assessment.
  • Claims of quantum advantage with no baseline, problem size or hardware stated.
  • No public reference document and no named sources.
  • A fixed date for when your industry will be disrupted.
  • A security recommendation that skips the inventory of what you use today.

Where another type is a better fit

  • Enterprise-wide implementation or systems integration across business units.
  • Proofs of concept on a particular vendor’s machine.
  • Pure cryptographic engineering work such as testing a specific library.

Questions

Which firms offer quantum computing consulting?

Strategy and management consultancies with a quantum practice, technology firms’ consulting arms, specialist advisers, and research groups and consortia all do. This guide names 14 of them by type, each described from its own page, and lists TQI Advisory separately as our practice. See the named list.

What do quantum computing consulting firms do?

They help organizations decide where to invest, which technologies to back, how to build capacity and how to prepare for the security risk. The work ranges from market and ecosystem studies and due diligence to cryptographic migration planning and proofs of concept on a specific machine.

What types of quantum computing consulting firms are there?

Five: global strategy and technology services firms, hardware and software vendors’ services arms, specialist intelligence and advisory firms, security and cryptography specialists, and academic or national laboratory groups. The right one depends on the decision you face.

Is a vendor’s consulting arm biased?

It has an interest in your choosing its platform, so test any technology recommendation against a vendor-neutral view. A vendor arm is often the right choice for a proof of concept once you have picked the platform.

Do I need a quantum consultant or a cybersecurity firm?

For the security risk, start with a cryptographic inventory, which a security specialist can run. For questions about where quantum computing could create value, you need someone who knows the technology and the market. See the Quantum Readiness Check for a first look at both.

How long does a quantum consulting engagement take?

It depends on the question. The TQI consulting page describes due diligence sprints as weeks, ecosystem assessments and economic impact studies as months, and retainers as continuous.

What does quantum consulting cost?

Prices vary with scope, and TQI Advisory scopes each engagement individually with no rate card. Ask any firm what is in the fee and what is not.
